New Bedford.wildlife_intro:
New Bedford is a working port city, and its wildlife profile is urban. Norway rats are the headline problem in the North and South End triple-deckers, following harbor, restaurant, and trash routes into basements and wall voids. Raccoons get into the attics and chimneys of mill-era multi-family homes, gray squirrels chew wiring in older West End houses, and bats roost in the eaves of whaling-era buildings near the waterfront. Skunks and opossums work the yards around Buttonwood Park and the Acushnet River corridor.

Unlike the Cape, New Bedford homes are occupied year-round, so calls come in waves tied to breeding seasons instead: raccoon denning in late winter, squirrel litters in spring and summer, and rodents pushing indoors in the fall. Our crew handles multi-family buildings as well as single homes — inspecting shared rooflines, sealing the gaps rats and squirrels actually use, and clearing attics under Massachusetts PAC rules. If you are hearing scratching tonight, call us and we will come out the same day.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in New Bedford?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, the building, and how many entry points a shared roofline or foundation has — triple-deckers often need more sealing than a single-family home. We inspect the building, show you the entry points we found, and quote the full job before starting. Call us to schedule an inspection.

faqs.q: We have rats in our triple-decker basement. Is sealing really the answer?
faqs.a: Yes — trapping alone never holds in mill-era buildings because new rats follow the same gaps at the foundation, sewer connections, and bulkhead. Our crew finds and seals those openings with materials rats cannot chew through, removes the animals inside under PAC rules, and advises on trash and food storage so the building stays clear.

Fall River.wildlife_intro:
Fall River's steep streets of triple-deckers produce a steady, urban wildlife workload. Norway rats move through the Flint, Maplewood, and South End along old foundations, covered sections of the Quequechan River, and restaurant trash routes. Bats roost in the attics of Highlands houses and older multi-family buildings, raccoons den in chimneys across the city, and gray squirrels get into soffits wherever mature street trees overhang the roofs. Skunks are common in yards near North Watuppa Pond and the state forest edge.

Because almost every Fall River home is occupied year-round, our work follows the animals' calendar: raccoon families in spring chimneys, bat colonies found in summer attics, squirrels and rats pushing inside in the fall. Our crew is used to multi-family buildings — we inspect the whole structure, seal shared entry points, and remove animals as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent. Massachusetts law does not allow moving trapped wildlife off the property, so durable sealing is what ends repeat calls. Call us for same-day service.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Fall River?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the species, the size of the building, and how much exclusion work the roofline and foundation need. Multi-family homes usually take more sealing than a single house. We inspect first and give one clear price for removal, sealing, and cleanup before any work begins — call us to book.

faqs.q: Can you just trap and take away the raccoons in our attic?
faqs.a: Massachusetts law prohibits relocating wildlife off the property where it was caught — trapped animals must be released on site or humanely euthanized, which is why trapping alone rarely solves an attic problem. Our crew's approach is exclusion: young are given time to leave with the mother, one-way exits are fitted where appropriate, and every entry point is sealed so the family cannot return.

Bats roost in the attics of mill-era homes in Weir Village and around the Green, Norway rats persist in the older downtown and riverfront blocks, and gray squirrels are a constant in the oak canopy over Whittenton and the postwar subdivisions.

Taunton homes are lived in year-round, so our crew works the full seasonal cycle: raccoon denning calls in late winter, bat and squirrel work through summer, and rodent exclusion in the fall as rats and mice push indoors. We work as a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent, with bat exclusion timed to the legal May and August-to-October windows. Call us for same-day service anywhere in Taunton.

faqs.a: The total depends on the animal involved, how it entered, and whether attic cleanup or foundation sealing is needed. faqs.q: Beavers are backing water up near our East Taunton road. What can be done?

Our crew can assess the site, walk you through the permit options, and carry out approved work such as a flow device or dam management where the permit allows.
